notes.summary: For any pseudoeffective zero-volume class and actual bounded reference type, proves a cocycle, concave raw energy independent of Kähler representatives, and leading relative energy limits along class-convergent auxiliary forms with bounded potentials. No fibration; P15.1 remains open.
notes.detailedSummary: The actual-current degree d<n is auxiliary-form independent, all same-type products above d vanish, and the degree-d energy has positive raw mass, an actual anchor, exact cocycles, constant shifts and sup-norm stability. Correct intrinsic Dirichlet IBP proves concavity, including an affine d=0 case. Its leading epsilon coefficient is independent of representatives, even for auxiliary classes converging without smooth representative convergence, provided moving potentials converge uniformly to a bounded-equivalent fixed potential. The differential-measure check requires a fixed or smoothly convergent full form and the sufficient o(epsilon) potential rate; it is not a P15.2 closure.
notes.text:
Partial P15.1 theorem, with no fibration hypothesis. Let X be a connected smooth compact Kähler n-fold, n>=1, alpha=[theta] pseudoeffective with vol(alpha)=0, and psi an actual theta-psh potential. Set dc=i(barpartial-partial)/(4pi), ddc=i partial barpartial/(2pi), T_u=theta+ddc u, and C_psi={u theta-psh: psi-C<=u<=psi+C for some C}. Differences and sup norms are taken off the common polar locus. This retains bounded singularity type, not merely ideal equivalence.

Foundations and checked scope. BEGZ, Acta Math. 205 (2010), 199–262, arXiv:0812.3674v2, Definition 1.1, Propositions 1.4 and 1.6, Theorem 1.8: actual-current nonpluripolar products on compact Kähler X are finite closed positive, symmetric, multilinear on positive sums, plurifinely local, and their traces have no pluripolar mass; smooth factors multiply ordinarily. DDNL, Anal. PDE 11 (2018), 2049–2087, Proposition 2.1: for n pseudoeffective smooth backgrounds, replacing each potential by one of the same bounded type preserves the top mixed integral. Theorem 2.4: making every potential less singular increases that integral. We apply these with k current slots and n-k smooth Kähler slots of potential zero, so the stated pseudoeffective hypotheses suffice. BEGZ Definition 1.17 defines big volume by minimal-singularity mass, gives the boundary limit vol(alpha+epsilon lambda)->vol(alpha), and identifies nef positive products with cup products. An arbitrary big-class actual-current mass is bounded above by volume by DDNL monotonicity; equality is never assumed.

Vu, arXiv:2005.13241v3 (25 March 2022), Lemmas 2.5–2.6 and Theorem 2.7: for a closed positive (n-1,n-1)-current R and bounded R-admissible dsh a,b, the intrinsic diagonal Dirichlet product is positive and
 integral b<ddc a dot-wedge R> = integral a<ddc b dot-wedge R> = -integral<db dc a dot-wedge R>.
Admissibility means a quasi-psh difference representation whose poles have zero R-mass. Proposition 2.1(iii) identifies iterated relative products with the ordinary products used here. Every R below is a nonpluripolar product times smooth positive closed factors, or is entirely smooth, so all differences and smooth tests are admissible and all products finite.

Convention and defect check: Vu's source operator is twice ours, so source potential u/2 represents the same current; DDNL uses i partial barpartial, so its source potential is u/(2pi). Positive rescaling preserves mass/type statements. Vu's source gradient of a/2 is half our gradient; multiplying source IBP by 2 gives the displayed formula. Intrinsically da dc a R=(1/2)ddc(a^2)R-a ddc a R. Vu v3 Eq. (2.3) has this correct 1/2, but repeated page-6/page-11 identities omit it. We preserve their raw quotations and never use those repetitions as definitions. The corrected local square coefficients are 1,1,-1/2. A direct cutoff check verifies the needed IBP: for negative quasi-psh representations a=phi1-phi2,b=phi3-phi4 with ddc phi_j>=-Omega, put chi_k=1+max(sum phi_j,-k)/k. Then 0<=chi_k<=1, ddc chi_k>=-4Omega/k, and correct bounded Stokes gives
 0<=integral dchi_k dcchi_k R=-integral chi_k ddc chi_k R<=4 integral Omega R/k.
The gradients of bounded difference truncations have mass <=2||a_k||_infty integral Omega R. Locality on {chi_k>0}, dominated convergence off the representation poles, and Cauchy–Schwarz make every cutoff cross term tend to zero. Bounded IBP therefore proves symmetry and the negative diagonal identity; polarization proves the full formula. Thus concavity below uses a positive intrinsic gradient, with the correct factor.

Define M_k=integral<T_psi^k>omega^(n-k), with M_0=integral omega^n, and d=max{k:M_k>0}. The carrier is X, of dimension n, and the nonpluripolar product has bidegree (d,d). The raw leading mass M_d is positive and is never normalized to one.

Degree proof. For epsilon>0, T_psi+epsilon omega is strictly positive and its class is big. Minimal singularities and DDNL monotonicity give
 0<=M_n<=P_epsilon:=integral<(T_psi+epsilon omega)^n><=vol(alpha+epsilon[omega]).
Actual-current multilinearity gives P_epsilon=sum_k binom(n,k) epsilon^(n-k) M_k. The volume bound tends to zero; hence M_n=0 and d<n. Any two Kähler forms are pointwise comparable, so their positive trace tests vanish for exactly the same degrees; d is auxiliary-form independent. DDNL bounded-type equality gives integral<T_u1...T_uk>omega^(n-k)=M_k for u_i in C_psi. For k>d this positive current has zero strictly positive trace and is therefore zero (its coefficient measures are dominated by its trace). Closedness makes M_k a cohomological polynomial of degree n-k in [omega]. There is no numerical-dimension identification.

Energy theorem. For lambda=[omega], r=n-d, define
 E_psi,lambda(u)=1/(d+1) sum_(a=0)^d integral (u-psi)<T_u^a T_psi^(d-a)>omega^r.
It is representative independent, increasing and concave, and satisfies
 E_psi(u)-E_psi(v)=E_v(u), E_psi(psi)=0,
 E_psi(u+c)=E_psi(u)+cM_d,
 |E_psi(u)-E_psi(v)|<=M_d||u-v||_infty.

Proof of the cocycle and variation, also valid at every fixed degree q with W=omega^(n-q), without the zero-volume assumption. On the convex hull of finitely many same-type potentials write u_t=u0+sum t_i h_i and A_i(t)=integral h_i<T_ut^q>W. These are polynomials with finite coefficient integrals. For q>=1, partial_j A_i=q integral h_i<ddc h_j T_ut^(q-1)>W is symmetric in i,j by the admissible IBP above; for q=0 the A_i are constant. Thus this polynomial one-form is closed. Its line integral from v to u equals
 integral_0^1 integral (u-v)<((1-t)T_v+tT_u)^q>W dt
 =1/(q+1)sum_a integral(u-v)<T_u^aT_v^(q-a)>W,
since binom(q,a) integral_0^1 t^a(1-t)^(q-a)dt=1/(q+1). Ordinary Stokes on the finite triangle psi,v,u proves the cocycle, including boundary points by polynomial continuity. Along u_t=(1-t)u+tv, h=v-u,
 E'(t)=integral h<T_ut^d>omega^r,
 E''(t)=-d integral<dh dc h dot-wedge (<T_ut^(d-1)>omega^r)><=0 for d>=1.
This is a polynomial identity with continuous endpoint derivatives. Pullbacks to finite simplices are polynomial and have the ordinary chain rule along C1/C2 parameter paths. No arbitrary unbounded or discontinuous velocity is covered. For d=0 the energy is affine and no gradient formula is asserted. Order, constant shifts, and the sandwiches v-delta<=u<=v+delta prove the remaining laws.

Representative independence proof. The compact Kähler ddc-lemma gives omega1-omega0=ddc g for cohomologous Kähler forms, with smooth real g. The exact used statement is that cohomologous smooth closed real (1,1)-forms on compact Kähler X differ by ddc of a smooth real function; a standard published reference is Deligne–Griffiths–Morgan–Sullivan, Invent. Math. 29 (1975), 245–274, §5, principle of two types. Expand omega1^r-omega0^r as ddc g sum_b omega1^b omega0^(r-1-b). For h=u-psi, Q=<T_u^aT_psi^(d-a)>, each R=Q omega1^b omega0^(r-1-b) is closed positive of degree n-1 with no representation-pole mass, also for d=0 when it is smooth. IBP gives integral h ddc g R=integral g<ddc h dot-wedge R>. The latter signed current is the difference of two degree-(d+1) products of same-type currents, both zero. This proves independence without illicit signed products. Changing one factor in a mixed product of r Kähler forms gives the same argument. Choosing fixed smooth representatives of a finite cohomology basis near any Kähler class makes the energy a homogeneous polynomial of degree r in that class, hence continuous. Changing theta to theta+ddc g and u,psi to u-g,psi-g changes no actual current or difference. Changing the actual anchor within its type has the cocycle, not absolute anchor independence.

Perturbative energy theorem. Define the unnormalized relative top energy in theta+epsilon omega, anchored at psi, by the analogous (n+1)-term sum, denoted E_epsilon,omega(v). It is defined for (theta+epsilon omega)-psh v of the bounded type psi; T_v alone need not be positive. The degree-n cocycle argument above applies to the positive perturbed currents and gives Lipschitz constant P_epsilon, the actual anchor mass. For fixed u in C_psi, write E_psi^(k),omega(u) for the degree-k relative sum. Actual-current expansion gives exactly
 E_epsilon,omega(u)=sum_(k=0)^d binom(n,k)epsilon^(n-k)E_psi^(k),omega(u),
 |E_psi^(k),omega(u)|<=||u-psi||_infty M_k.
The mixed-sum coefficient identity is sum_j binom(j,a)binom(n-j,k-a)=binom(n+1,k+1), proved by marking the (a+1)-st member of a (k+1)-subset of {0,...,n}; division by n+1 gives binom(n,k)/(k+1).

Let ANY Kähler forms omega_epsilon have [omega_epsilon]->lambda, with lambda Kähler, without representative convergence. If u_epsilon is perturbed-psh, of the same bounded type, and ||u_epsilon-u||_infty=delta_epsilon->0 for a fixed u in C_psi, then
 E_epsilon,omega_epsilon(u_epsilon)/(binom(n,d)epsilon^(n-d))->E_psi,lambda(u).
Indeed the replacement error is <=delta_epsilon P_epsilon. The M_k are bounded cohomological polynomials on a compact neighborhood of lambda, so P_epsilon=O(epsilon^(n-d)) uniformly. The normalized k<d terms are O(epsilon^(d-k)); the leading energy is representative independent and class-continuous. This is only a leading-coefficient assertion. The full positive-epsilon energy can depend on representatives: on P1xP1, theta=p1*kappa, psi=0, u=p1*v smooth nonconstant, omega0=p1*kappa+p2*kappa, replacing omega0 by omega0+t ddc u changes its degree-zero coefficient by -2t integral dv dc v, although the leading degree-one coefficient is unchanged.

Auxiliary differential check, not a P15.2 claim. For a fixed omega, the measure expansion gives <(T_u+epsilon omega)^n>/(binom(n,d)epsilon^(n-d))-><T_u^d>omega^r. For moving same-type u_epsilon, factor the difference into n signed mixed terms. Smooth-test IBP bounds each by C_f delta_epsilon times the mixed mass with one omega factor. DDNL bounded-type equality identifies that mass with Q_epsilon=sum_(k=0)^d binom(n-1,k)epsilon^(n-1-k)M_k=O(epsilon^(r-1)). Therefore the normalized test error is O_f(delta_epsilon/epsilon); o(epsilon) is a sufficient potential rate. This includes n=1,d=0 using the empty product. Smoothly convergent positive auxiliary forms permit uniform constants. Merely class-convergent forms do not supply the needed test bound or a full-form-free measure limit.

Full proofs, applicability checks and immutable source bodies are in P15.1-argument.md; the new proof is also in standalone P15.1-partial.tex and its twice-compiled PDF. Original P15.1 remains open outside the stated scope. Rerun: python build.py. No compilation or finite arithmetic result certifies the analytic theorem.

notes.summary: Proves a genuine more-singular relative full-mass, finite joint linear-weight extension: exact capped truncation integrals, decreasing continuity, finite cocycles, concavity and same-type/fixed-class reference changes. No unbounded perturbation theorem.
notes.detailedSummary: Using Vu v3 convexity with exact source hypotheses, every finite-family degree-d mixed product has full mass and integrable joint weights. Locality plus equal mass makes each truncation weighted integral exactly a capped integral against the limiting mixed measure. This yields the finite energy, independence of all decreasing bounded-type approximants, decreasing monotone continuity, mixed cocycles and bounded anchor changes. Fixed auxiliary-class representative independence passes through truncations. A sublogarithmic singularity example proves the domain genuinely includes unbounded differences. Increasing-sequence continuity and unbounded variations/path limits are not asserted.
notes.text:
Genuine finite-energy extension of n1, with exactly decreasing monotone continuity. Keep X,theta,psi,d,r,lambda,omega and M=M_d from n1. For d>=1, define F^1_psi,lambda by u theta-psh, u<=psi+C, integral<T_u^d>omega^r=M, and
 sum_a binom(d,a) integral |u-psi|<T_u^aT_psi^(d-a)>omega^r<infinity.
For d=0 use u<=psi+C and integral|u-psi|omega^n<infinity; the latter follows from local integrability of quasi-psh functions and degree-zero full mass is automatic. Define E_psi,lambda(u) by the same (d+1)-term relative sum as n1.

Additional foundations, with exact application. Vu arXiv:2005.13241v3 §3 defines full relative mass by equality of cohomology classes of relative products. For P=T_psi, m=d and T=omega^r, these products are top degree and X connected, so equality is equality of scalar masses. For normalized negative u<=psi, his Eq. (3.1) with chi(t)=t is exactly d sum_a binom(d,a) integral(psi-u)<T_u^aT_psi^(d-a)>omega^r. Thus the above domain is precisely his diagonal joint linear-weight class. Theorem 3.4 states that both this weighted class and its full-mass class are convex; Corollary 3.2 makes the weighted class invariant under replacing P by a cohomologous current of the same bounded type. These are used as standard foundations with their exact hypotheses; their printed proofs by reference are not newly reconstructed. The source convention conversion in n1 changes weight by a positive constant and preserves finiteness. The source product and comparison-set locality, including unbounded comparison potentials, are Vu Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 3.3. No minimal-reference or model-envelope assumption is inserted.

Mixed masses and weights. Normalize any finite family u_i<=psi. Its average w belongs to the weighted full-mass class by convexity. Expanding <T_w^d>omega^r expresses its mass M as the average of N^d nonnegative ordered mixed masses. Every summand is <=M by DDNL monotonicity toward psi, with r smooth slots, so every summand equals M. The finite a=d term for w gives integral(psi-w)<T_w^d>omega^r<infinity; positive expansion and 0<=psi-u_i<=N(psi-w) prove integrability of every psi-u_i against every degree-d mixed product in this family. In particular all |u-v|-weighted products <T_u^aT_v^(d-a)>omega^r are integrable. Additive constants reverse the normalization. All polar sets have zero product mass. For d=0 the assertions are smooth-volume integrability. DDNL monotonicity also kills every degree k>d product of more-singular members; it gives no lower-degree weighted bound.

Exact truncation proof. For u<=psi, let z=psi-u, u_L=max(u,psi-L), mu_a=<T_u^aT_psi^(d-a)>omega^r and mu_a,L=<T_uL^aT_psi^(d-a)>omega^r. Both masses are M. On G_L={u>psi-L}, locality makes the measures equal. On B_L, the truncated weight psi-u_L is exactly L; equal total masses give mu_a,L(B_L)=mu_a(B_L). Therefore
 integral(psi-u_L)dmu_a,L=integral min(z,L)dmu_a.
Boundary equality sets are harmless because the weight is constant there; poles have zero mass. Monotone convergence gives E(u_L) decreasing to the finite displayed energy. This proves existence and independence of any real levels tending to infinity. Ordered potentials have ordered truncations, so E is increasing; all mixed masses equal M, so constant shifts are cM.

Bounded decreasing continuity needed for the extension. The standard scalar capacity fact is that decreasing quasi-psh functions in a fixed background, with a non-identically-minus-infinity quasi-psh limit, converge in Kähler capacity (Guedj–Zeriahi 2005, Proposition 3.7 as cited in the supplied DDNL Theorem 2.4 proof, p.2057). DDNL Proposition 2.2 states that uniformly bounded local psh potentials converging in capacity, multiplied by uniformly bounded quasicontinuous weights converging in capacity, have convergent weighted Bedford–Taylor top products. Quasi-psh functions and bounded truncations are quasicontinuous. These are standard foundations; the big-class-only DDNL Theorem 2.3 is not applied to the pseudoeffective background.

Here is the full tail argument: if v_j decreases to v with all differences from psi bounded uniformly by B, all mixed products of v_j,psi and fixed smooth slots have the same mass m as the limiting product. Put eta_L=min(1,max(psi+L,0)). On its nonzero set the potentials plus smooth local theta-potentials have uniform lower bounds, so replace them by uniformly bounded local psh truncations. Locality preserves the product there. Capacity convergence and Proposition 2.2 give convergence both of integral eta_L dnu_j and of integral eta_L(v_j-psi)dnu_j, using a smooth partition of unity. These are strictly local bounded applications in every current slot. The omitted weighted integral is bounded by B integral(1-eta_L)dnu_j. Since total masses equal m, this tail tends, for fixed L, to B integral(1-eta_L)dnu. Let L tend to infinity; the latter tends to zero because nu has no polar mass. Thus the entire bounded energy converges, even with unbounded psi.

For arbitrary v_j in F^1 decreasing to u in F^1, monotonicity gives E(u)<=E(v_j)<=E(max(v_j,psi-L)). For fixed L the upper potentials converge within a uniform bounded type and the preceding lemma applies. Taking j to infinity and then L to infinity proves E(v_j)->E(u). In particular every decreasing bounded-type approximation of u has the same value. Concavity follows by taking simultaneous truncations u_L,v_L: their convex combinations decrease to (1-t)u+tv, which belongs to the domain by Vu convexity, so decreasing continuity passes bounded concavity to the limit. For d=0 the formula is affine. No increasing-sequence or unbounded-velocity theorem is claimed.

Cocycle proof. Normalize u,v<=psi and truncate both at L. Put nu_a=<T_u^aT_v^(d-a)>omega^r and nu_a,L for the truncated pair. They have equal mass M and agree on G_L={u>psi-L,v>psi-L}. On the complement B_L, |u_L-v_L|<=L and equal complementary masses imply
 integral_B_L |u_L-v_L|dnu_a,L<=L nu_a(B_L)<=integral_B_L[(psi-u)+(psi-v)]dnu_a->0.
The original |u-v| tail also tends to zero by mixed weight integrability. The weights and products agree on G_L. Thus the bounded pair energy tends to the finite pair sum 1/(d+1)sum_a integral(u-v)<T_u^aT_v^(d-a)>omega^r. Passing to the bounded cocycle proves E_psi(u)-E_psi(v)=E_v(u). Constants handle the general normalization.

Reference changes. Vu Corollary 3.2 gives the same domain for psi' bounded-equivalent to psi; bounded mixed-mass equality gives the same d,M. With u_L truncated against psi, mixed products of u_L and psi' agree with the untruncated products on {u>psi-L} and have equal total mass. On the complement their truncated absolute weight is <=L+||psi-psi'||_infty, whose integral tends to zero by the finite-family weight argument. This passes the bounded anchor identity to E_psi'(u)=E_psi(u)-E_psi(psi'). For another Kähler representative omega' of the same lambda, closedness/cohomology preserves full mass and pointwise comparison preserves finiteness of each absolute weighted integral. Taking limits of representative-independent bounded energies proves representative independence of E. Smooth-background gauge changes are unchanged actual currents as in n1. No minimum quotient across auxiliary classes is asserted for this unbounded domain.

The domain truly includes unbounded differences. On P1xP1, theta=p1*kappa, psi=0, omega=p1*kappa+p2*kappa with integral kappa=1, take u=p1*v, where v=-b(-log|z|)^a near zero, 0<a<1/2. A smooth cutoff away from zero and small b ensure kappa+ddc v>=0: the singular radial Hessian is positive and the cutoff Hessian is bounded on a fixed annulus. Its density is a positive constant times r^(-2)(-log r)^(a-2), with boundary flux proportional to (-log r)^(a-1)->0, so it has no polar atom and has mass 1. The singular weighted integral is proportional to integral^infinity t^(2a-2)dt<infinity, and v is integrable against smooth kappa. Thus both joint terms are finite, full degree-one mass holds, and u is unbounded. This example demonstrates the extension; the theorem itself assumes no product/fibration.

The full proof and source bodies are in P15.1-argument.md and the new proof in P15.1-partial.tex/PDF. These are scoped partial results; unbounded perturbation limits are not implied. Rerun: python build.py.

notes.summary: Analytic counterexample: fixed-class auxiliary representatives can make rescaled positive-perturbation relative energies diverge for one fixed, full-mass finite-energy unbounded potential. Refutes an unbounded strengthening, not P15.1 itself.
notes.detailedSummary: On P1 x P1 with the pullback nef zero-volume class, a sublogarithmic base potential has finite degree-one energy and full mass. Smooth positive auxiliary forms in one fixed Kähler class concentrate a half-mass bump in radius exp(-epsilon^(-2/a)). The potential has finite full relative top energy at each positive epsilon, yet the rescaled energy equals its finite leading energy plus epsilon times its integral against the concentrating base form, which tends to minus infinity. A fixed smooth representative instead gives the finite leading limit. The bounded theorem is unaffected; uniform lower weighted-coefficient control cannot be deduced from degree-d finite energy.
notes.text:
Analytic counterexample to extending n1's class-convergent auxiliary-path limit to every finite-energy unbounded potential; it is not a refutation of P15.1 in its entirety.

Use X=P1xP1, normalized Fubini–Study kappa, theta=p1*kappa, psi=0, and the fixed potential u=p1*v from n2, with v<=0 and v(z)=-b(-log|z|)^a near zero, 0<a<1/2. This is a nef pseudoeffective zero-volume class since theta^2=0, and the actual reference has d=1, M_1=1. The potential has finite degree-one joint energy and full mass, as proved by the radial density and flux calculation in n2.

Let rho_epsilon=exp(-epsilon^(-2/a)). Choose a nonnegative smooth two-form beta_epsilon of integral 1 supported in |z|<rho_epsilon, by rescaling a disk bump and extending by zero. On P1 it is closed. Put kappa_epsilon=(kappa+beta_epsilon)/2 and omega_epsilon=p1*kappa_epsilon+p2*kappa. These are smooth Kähler forms with precisely one fixed cohomology class lambda, because integrals determine H^2(P1,R). No smooth convergence occurs. Keep u_epsilon=u exactly.

Write S=kappa+ddc v, positive of mass 1 and without a polar atom. Then T_u=p1*S, and T_u+epsilon omega_epsilon is positive. For each fixed epsilon, v is integrable against the smooth kappa_epsilon, and against S and kappa by n2. Every positive-perturbation joint weighted integral is finite. Nonpluripolar products agree with the following rank-one expansions off the polar fiber and have no polar mass:
 anchor square =2epsilon p1*(kappa+epsilon kappa_epsilon)p2*kappa;
 mixed term =epsilon p1*(S+kappa+2epsilon kappa_epsilon)p2*kappa;
 u square =2epsilon p1*(S+epsilon kappa_epsilon)p2*kappa.
The u square and anchor square both have mass 2epsilon(1+epsilon). Thus the fixed u is full-mass and finite-energy relative to every positive perturbation, not merely in the limiting degree-one theory.

Averaging the three weighted terms gives exactly
 E_epsilon,omega_epsilon(u)=2epsilon E_0,lambda(u)+2epsilon^2 integral v kappa_epsilon,
 E_0,lambda(u)=(1/2)integral v(S+kappa) finite.
This expansion is legitimate for the unbounded potential because each displayed weighted integral is finite at that fixed parameter; no unproved unbounded IBP is used.

On the bump support, -v>=b epsilon^(-2), and therefore integral v kappa_epsilon<=-(b/2)epsilon^(-2). Consequently
 E_epsilon,omega_epsilon(u)/(2epsilon)=E_0,lambda(u)+epsilon integral v kappa_epsilon -> -infinity.
Using instead the fixed smooth omega=p1*kappa+p2*kappa, the same expression tends to the finite E_0,lambda(u), because integral v kappa is fixed and finite. Both paths use exactly the same auxiliary class and exactly the same potential at every parameter.

This satisfies every ambient hypothesis and proves a failure of the proposed unbounded strengthening. It does not contradict the bounded theorem, which controls lower weighted coefficients by ||u-psi||_infty times bounded cohomological masses. Here all lower weighted coefficients are finite at each epsilon but fail uniform control. Even full relative top mass and finite positive-perturbation energy at every epsilon do not repair that failure. A further uniform-integrability condition, a restriction on representatives, or another limiting prescription would require its own theorem. No such condition is silently inserted into original P15.1. Complete calculations are in P15.1-argument.md and P15.1-partial.tex/PDF; no numerical simulation is needed.

notes.summary: Characterizes the coarsest reference-scale equivalence for the bounded energy family, gives scale/type examples, and records verified source/build evidence and concrete remaining P15.1 gaps. Status partial; candidate false.
notes.detailedSummary: Mixed auxiliary-class energies define linear functionals on Sym^(n-d) H^(1,1); their common kernel characterizes exactly when two formal scale tensors give the same whole bounded energy family. Product examples show a raw scale matters and actual reference degree can differ within one class. This characterization does not certify a universal minimal reference for all unbounded domains or supply a lower-dimensional geometric carrier. All 14 supplied LF pins match; printed source defects are preserved and corrected only in new calculations. TeX compiles twice and exact coefficient diagnostics pass, neither of which establishes analytic correctness. Original input strings remain intact; no network, extra models, subagents or heavy compute are used.
notes.text:
Reference-scale characterization, exact residual scope, and artifact evidence; uses n1–n3 and does not claim original closure.

For the bounded family of actual type tau=[psi], put V=H^(1,1)(X,R), r=n-d. Replacing omega^r in the pair-energy formula by omega1...omega_r defines a symmetric multilinear functional L_u,v on r Kähler classes. Independence of each representative follows exactly as in n1: changing one factor inserts ddc g, the remaining factors are closed positive, admissible IBP transfers ddc to u-v, and degree-(d+1) current vanishing makes it zero. Extend to arbitrary classes by writing a smooth representative eta as (eta+C Omega)-C Omega, with both forms Kähler. Multilinearity and the same representative-change argument in each remaining factor make this extension independent of the decomposition. Thus L_u,v defines a linear functional ell_u,v on Sym^r V. Set K_tau=intersection_(u,v in C_psi)ker ell_u,v. Two formal scale tensors yield the same entire bounded relative-energy family exactly when their difference lies in K_tau. Hence the image of lambda^(symmetric r) in Sym^r V/K_tau is the coarsest scale-equivalence datum for this bounded family. The actual anchor gives an additive origin; bounded anchor changes obey the cocycle. This is a proved bounded-family characterization, not a claim that an entire Kähler class is always minimal, or a universal minimal reference for unbounded domains.

Examples establish necessity and type sensitivity. On P1xP1, theta=p1*kappa, psi=0, omega=A p1*kappa+B p2*kappa, integral kappa=1, A,B>0: d=1, M_1=B, and E(c)=cB. Some scale cannot be discarded. Bounded theta-psh potentials are constant on each second-factor compact fiber by the psh maximum principle, so they descend to the first factor; their energies involve B alone, showing redundant auxiliary data may exist. For the actual reference psi=p1*log(|z|^2/(1+|z|^2)), ddc log|z|^2=delta_0 by boundary flux and ddc log(1+|z|^2)=kappa. Thus T_psi is the vertical divisor current and its nonpluripolar first product is zero: it is entirely on its polar divisor. Its actual degree is d=0, in the same class whose smooth reference has d=1. The nef class numerical dimension is 1, so actual-reference degree is not class numerical dimension. Moreover actual perturbed mass is 2AB epsilon^2, whereas nef class volume is 2B epsilon+2AB epsilon^2. A class-volume leading exponent would annihilate the actual constant-shift energy after rescaling. This explicitly prevents substitution of class-volume asymptotics for actual-reference mass without a separate theorem.

All integrals have carrier X of dimension n, with a degree-d nonpluripolar current; no geometric d-dimensional quotient/carrier is constructed. Bounded energy needs the stated class or quotient; its differential measure generally needs the full form. The finite-energy extension has fixed-class representative invariance, but no across-class minimum characterization is claimed there.

Original P15.1 remains open. The proved domains are bounded actual type and more-singular relative full-mass finite joint linear-weight potentials. Decreasing monotone continuity, cocycles, concavity and fixed-class reference changes are proved in n2; arbitrary increasing continuity and unbounded velocity/path calculus are not.
